newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks stagnate as buyers holiday.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks stagnate as buyers holiday.

text.p: Most Croatian stocks stagnated at midday on Friday as buyers stayed away for an extended May 1 Labour Day holiday, market participants said.
"It's dead still today with very few transactions and volumes are minimal," said one trader with a large market share.
He mentioned only one large deal by 1230 (1030 GMT) involving 600 shares in food concern Podravka at 304 kuna -- one down from Wednesday's close.

Blue chip drugs firm Pliva was weaker at around 481 kuna on volume of 100 shares. Its 1/5 global depositary receipts (GDRs) earlier dipped to $16.21 each from Thursday's close at $16.4 on the London Stock Exchange.
Shares in Zagrebacka Banka rose to 2,200 from 2,183 kuna they ended at before the market break.

But negligible volume provided no reliable indication on whether the current strength would be maintained until the bank closes its shareholder register -- probably two weeks before the June 10 annual meeting.
Zagrebacka's GDRs fetched $35.87-$36 on London's Seaq International. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
